name: Great Yarmouth

licensing.selective: Selective licensing covers privately rented homes in Central and Northgate, Nelson, Southtown and Cobholm, and Yarmouth North wards, from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. After a challenge by landlords in 2026 the council withdrew a set of extra licence conditions, but the scheme stays in place.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme is listed: larger HMOs (five or more people from two or more households) need a national mandatory licence.
licensing.fee: £694 per self-contained home for a five-year selective licence (2026)

housing: Great Yarmouth is a seaside and port town at the mouth of the Yare, with Gorleston across the river and a string of coastal and Broads villages. The central wards have dense Victorian terraces and large former guest houses, many converted into flats and shared homes, and a high share of private renting; this is where the selective licensing scheme applies. Gorleston and Bradwell have more interwar and post-war family housing, while the villages are mostly bungalows and holiday homes. Private renting grew faster than the regional average between 2011 and 2021.
checkinTips: Former guest houses near the seafront converted into flats: photograph each flat's door, meters, fire doors, alarms and the shared hallway.
Coastal homes: look for salt corrosion on window frames, door furniture and outside metalwork, and damp on exposed walls.
Low-lying homes in Southtown and Cobholm: look for signs of past flooding or damp in ground-floor rooms.
Victorian terraces in Northgate and the town centre: check for damp at the base of walls and in rear kitchens, and photograph yards and rear access.
Bungalows and chalets in Hemsby and Caister: record the roof, windows and heating, and note any coastal erosion warnings for the area.
Homes in the selective licensing wards: note the licence number and check the licence conditions on smoke alarms and gas safety are met.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Great Yarmouth Borough Council's private sector housing team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
